$doc: The wire contract between the TypeScript server and the C++ bridge plugin, declared once. scripts/generate-wire-contract.mjs writes src/bridge/wire-contract.ts, scripts/lib/wire-contract.mjs and the plugin's MCPWireContract.h from this file and runtime.ts.tmpl; npm run generate runs it and the generated drift gate fails CI on a stale output. Change values additively: an installed bridge or client built from an older copy of this file keeps reading the wire.

protocol.doc: Wire protocol version, reported by get_bridge_capabilities. Version 1 is every bridge built before the handshake existed; those answer it with Unknown method. Version 2 reassembles messages across reads and frames, answers close and ping frames, validates the upgrade request and serves the handshake. Bump it when a change would make an older client misread the wire.

handlerApi.doc: Native handler ABI version for plugins that register their own handlers. Bump it when the handler signature or registration contract changes in a breaking way. 2: external handlers can register a parameter contract (MCPHandlerSpec.h). 3: the spec structs gain parameter defaults and action facts (FMCPActionFacts: timeout, modal safety, batch refusal, server-internal caller), which changes their layout, so a plugin built against 2 is rebuilt.

features.doc: Capability names get_bridge_capabilities advertises. A client asks about the one thing it needs instead of comparing version numbers. Every name is always compiled in and always advertised.

jsonRpcErrors.doc: JSON-RPC 2.0 error codes the bridge answers with.

bridgeErrorCodes.doc: errorCode values a handler answers with that the client keys behaviour on.

routingParams.doc: Parameter names the dispatcher consumes before a call reaches a handler. Never a handler argument, and never reported as an unread parameter.

maxCalls.doc: The most steps one editor(batch) call carries. The whole list runs as one game-thread job, so this bounds how long one call holds the editor; a longer edit is two batches.

defaultSeconds.doc: How long the bridge waits on the game thread for an action that declares no timeout of its own (FMCPActionFacts::TimeoutSeconds). get_bridge_capabilities.actionFacts lists every action that declares one.

maxRequestSeconds.doc: The most a call's timeoutMs can raise its budget to. A larger value is capped here, never refused; work that needs longer is split into several calls, or run through the action's job form and polled where it has one.

bridgeState.doc: The state a bridge record reports. A bind-failed record names no reachable port: it exists to explain a failure, not to be dialled.

dialogRefusal.doc: The answer every method that is not modal-safe gets while a modal dialog is up. The client builds the call that presses a button from buttonLabel, so the bridge never spells tool syntax.

stateDir.doc: Where the bridge and the client exchange records, under the project directory (not ProjectSavedDir, which -UserDir moves).

portLockfile.doc: port.json: the port the project's editor bound. Written temp-and-rename by the instance that bound it, removed only by that instance. Read for its port and pid; an older bridge writes no pid.

instance.doc: instances/<pid>.json: one editor's own record of the bridge it runs or failed to run. One writer per file by construction.

bridgeError.doc: bridge-error.json: what a start that could not bind leaves behind, so editor alive and bridge dead is distinguishable from no editor.

requestedPort.doc: requested.json: the port pin the client resolved, written by the client and read by the bridge. It exists only while a pin exists, and carries an integer, never a policy.

installKind.doc: How the running plugin was installed, from its install marker.

token.doc: The bridge's per-session token: published by the plugin to <dir>/<port><suffix>, readable only by the editor's user, and required on every WebSocket upgrade as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

canvasReservedPorts.doc: Ports the Unreal Canvas Bridge claims when a project enables it. A pin on one falls back to the derived port, and the collision walk steps over them.

checkpointManifest.doc: One line of a checkpoint generation's manifest.jsonl: a file that was about to be written, whether it existed, and where its prior bytes were copied. A line without a version field is version 1; a reader skips lines newer than it knows.

env.doc: Environment variables the plugin reads. Each is also in src/core/env.ts, which documents every variable the server reads.

port.doc: The bridge port. Each project derives its own from a hash of its root, so checkouts on one machine do not collide and neither side has to coordinate: SHA-1 (available to both Node and Unreal; spreading only, never security) of the normalized root, first four bytes big-endian, folded into [base, base + span). Normalized means forward slashes, no trailing slash, lowercase. The port.json the bridge publishes stays the authority on the port actually bound.
